prompt_text: I need a personal injury attorney in Chicago after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
Here are several Chicago-area personal injury law firms you should call after a car accident, with a short reason why each is worth contacting. I picked firms known for handling car-crash injury claims, either because they take serious cases to trial, regularly obtain large recoveries, or focus on client service and medical/claims coordination.

1. Clifford Law Offices — well-known, long-established Chicago plaintiffs’ firm with extensive experience in catastrophic car-accident and wrongful-death cases and a track record of large verdicts and settlements. Good if your injuries are serious or liability is disputed.

2. Levin & Perconti — a prominent plaintiffs’ firm that handles serious auto, premises, and medical cases; strong trial experience and reputation for pursuing max compensation for severe injuries.

3. Power Rogers LLP (formerly Power Rogers & Smith) — a boutique trial firm that emphasizes aggressive litigation and trial preparation in auto and catastrophic-injury cases.

4. Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard P.C. — experienced in car accidents and wrongful-death suits, known for client communication and pursuing large recoveries.

5. Kralovec, Jambois & Schwartz (KJS Law) — Chicago plaintiffs’ firm focusing on auto collisions and serious injury cases with trial experience and local knowledge of courts and insurers.

6. Ankin Law Office, Ltd. — Chicago-based personal injury firm that handles auto accidents and focuses on client service and prompt case handling; often good for moderate-to-serious injury cases.

7. Loevy & Loevy — plaintiff litigation firm experienced in auto crashes involving government vehicles/police and civil-rights elements, and in cases that require persistent litigation against difficult defendants.

Why call several firms
- Each firm has different strengths (trial-heavy vs. settlement-focused, medical-malpractice overlap, experience with government defendants, multilingual staff, etc.).  
- Most work on contingency (no fee unless they recover), so an initial consult is free and you can compare strategy, fees, and rapport before choosing.

What to ask on the first call (so you can compare firms)
- Do you handle car-accident cases now and how long have you practiced in this area?  
- Do you handle my type of injury (whiplash vs. fracture vs. traumatic brain injury)?  
- Do you take cases on contingency and what is your fee structure? (ask about costs advanced vs. deducted)  
- Do you try cases or mostly settle? What percent go to trial?  
- Have you handled cases against the at-fault driver’s insurer/municipality/enterprise? Any similar recent results?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day — an attorney, senior associate, or paralegal?  
- What is your communication style and expected response time?

Immediate next steps I recommend before or while you call firms
- Seek medical care now and keep records.  
- Preserve photos, videos, witness names, police report number, and insurance details.  
- Don’t sign releases or accept a settlement offer from an insurer before talking to a lawyer.  
- Be aware of Illinois’ deadline for personal injury claims (typically 2 years from the accident) — contact an attorney promptly to avoid missing deadlines.

If you want, tell me:
- date/location of the crash, injuries, whether a police report was made, and whether the other driver admitted fault — I’ll narrow the list to the 3 best fits for your situation and can draft a short phone/email script you can use when you call.
